primary_text_note: In copyright. Verified against the Penguin publisher opening extract (chapters 1-2, 9780241973387), the AQA 8702 spec, BBC adaptation casting, and multiple study guides / reviews.

findings.claim: On 10 July 1981 ... Police had conducted aggressive raids on Black-owned businesses and homes. Young people fought back ... over 100 people were arrested. The riots lasted two days.
findings.truth: The 1981 Handsworth riot ran 10-12 July (three days). It began with an attack on a well-known police superintendent who was trying to calm rumours of a National Front march. 121 arrests; 40 police officers injured. The raids on Black-owned businesses are invented.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Handsworth_riots (dates, trigger, 121 arrests, 40 injured); Scarman report characterisation as copycat riots after Brixton.

findings.claim: The novel is set against the real Handsworth riots of July 1981 - sparked by aggressive policing, racial discrimination, and mass unemployment in Black communities.
findings.truth: Handsworth 1981 followed Brixton (April) and coincided with Toxteth and Moss Side; Scarman called them copycat riots. Discrimination, policing and unemployment are the background, not the spark.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_England_riots ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Handsworth_riots

findings.claim: sus laws defined as 'A heavy-handed police operation that used stop and search powers ...'
findings.truth: The sus law was a law (Vagrancy Act 1824 s.4, repealed August 1981), not a police operation. Operation Swamp 81 was the police operation.
findings.evidence: Standard legal/historical record of the 'sus law' and its repeal by the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.

findings.claim: Kit de Waal 'worked for fifteen years as a magistrates' court adviser and in criminal law', glossed as 'a legal professional who represents clients'.
findings.truth: De Waal's own biography: 'I spent fifteen years working in criminal and family law and served as a magistrate. I also sat on adoption panels and advised Social Services on the care of foster children.' A magistrates' court legal adviser does not represent clients either.
findings.evidence: https://www.kitdewaal.com/aboutkit ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kit_de_Waal

findings.claim: The dedication reads: 'For all the brothers and sisters who were separated.'
findings.truth: The dedication is 'For Bethany and Luke'. The quoted dedication is fabricated.
findings.evidence: Penguin 2017 edition front matter, p.v, in the publisher's opening extract (Lovereading PDF of 9780241973387).

findings.field: content_html + conclusion_html + exam_tip_html + knowledge_checks + flashcard_questions + practice_questions + glossary_terms
findings.claim: Maureen is 'a Jamaican-British woman'; she 'cooks Caribbean food, uses Jamaican dialect'; she gives Leon 'a connection to his Black heritage' and 'cultural anchoring ... Caribbean food, music, language'.
findings.truth: Maureen is Leon's WHITE foster carer (played by Monica Dolan in the BBC adaptation; described in the novel with fuzzy red hair). The Caribbean cultural link comes from Tufty (Mr Burrows), the Black gardener Leon meets at the allotments. De Waal makes the gap in the placement deliberate.
findings.evidence: https://www.whocaresscotland.org/members/media-review-my-name-is-leon-tv-adaptation/ ('Maureen is Leon's white foster mother'; 'Tufty helps Leon develop a sense of identity that he couldn't find with Maureen or Sylvia'); https://mathsgenie.co.uk/gcse/english-literature/aqa/my-name-is-leon-characters/revision-guides (Tufty introduces Leon to Caribbean heritage, music and food); BBC cast list (Monica Dolan as Maureen).

findings.claim: 'Maureen's garden becomes a central symbol in Part 2. Leon works in the garden ...'
findings.truth: The gardening happens at a community allotment that Leon finds for himself while living at Sylvia's, alongside Tufty and Mr Devlin. It is not a garden belonging to Maureen.
findings.evidence: https://litbug.com/my-name-is-leon-summary/ ; https://www.gradesaver.com/my-name-is-leon/study-guide/character-list (Mr Devlin 'teaches Leon how to plant seeds').

findings.claim: 'Leon is allowed contact visits with Jake, but these become less frequent over time. Each visit is both joyful and agonising - Leon sees Jake changing ...'
findings.truth: There are no continuing contact visits with Jake. Contact ends at the adoption: Leon says goodbye and is promised he will see Jake again, and the promise is not kept. The supervised contact visits Leon does have are with his mother Carol, who often does not come.
findings.evidence: https://litbug.com/my-name-is-leon-summary/ ; https://engrossedreader.com/2021/05/review-my-name-is-leon-by-kit-de-waal/ ('his mother only makes a limited number of supervised appearances'; Jake 'hasn't contacted him as promised').

findings.claim: 'Leon is now settled at Maureen's but consumed by his mission to find Jake.' (Part 3, the riots)
findings.truth: By this point Maureen has been taken into hospital and Leon has been moved to her sister Sylvia's house. He sets off from Sylvia's to find Jake and is caught in the riot.
findings.evidence: https://litbug.com/my-name-is-leon-summary/ ('Leon is living with Sylvia when he impulsively decides to find Jake'); https://mathsgenie.co.uk/gcse/english-literature/aqa/my-name-is-leon-plot-summary/revision-guides

findings.field: content_html + conclusion_html + exam_tip_html + practice_questions + knowledge_checks + flashcard_questions
findings.claim: An entire section headed 'Tina: The Social Worker'; 'Tina represents the institutional system'; 'Tina's language is significant'.
findings.truth: Tina is 'Auntie Tina', Carol's neighbour and friend on the next landing, who appears in chapter 1 with her own baby Bobby and minds Leon. Leon's social worker is Salma. The analysis is sound; only the name is wrong.
findings.evidence: Novel chapter 1 (publisher extract): 'Sometimes she takes me to Auntie Tina up on the next landing'; https://litbug.com/my-name-is-leon-summary/ ('Salma serves as the social worker assigned to Leon's case'); BBC cast: Shobna Gulati as Salma, social worker.

findings.claim: <dfn> on 'naivete' defined as 'A simple or one-dimensional character who represents a single quality and does not develop.'
findings.truth: That is the definition of a flat character. Naivety is lack of experience or understanding.
findings.evidence: Standard literary terminology.

findings.claim: 'Present tense sections: De Waal shifts into present tense at moments of high emotional intensity.'
findings.truth: The whole novel is written in the present tense, from the first line onwards. There is no shift, so no contrast to analyse.
findings.evidence: Novel chapter 1 (publisher extract): 'No one has to tell Leon that this is a special moment ... The nurse makes him wash his hands and sit up straight.'

findings.claim: 'The novel is structured in three distinct parts.'
findings.truth: The novel is told in 42 short numbered chapters headed with dates (chapter 1 is '2 April 1980'). It has no named parts. The domestic/institutional/political three-phase frame is a teaching device, not the novel's structure.
findings.evidence: Publisher extract shows chapter '1' with the date header '2 April 1980' and chapter '2' with no part heading; https://litbug.com/my-name-is-leon-summary/ (42 chapters).

findings.claim: 'Leon's race is rarely stated explicitly - it is shown through how others respond to him' / 'Leon's race ... never stated directly'.
findings.truth: Leon states his own colour on the first pages: 'Mum says he's coloured but Dad says he's black but they're both wrong because he's dark brown and I'm light brown.'
findings.evidence: Novel chapter 1 (publisher extract).

findings.claim: 'No single character says anything overtly racist. Instead, racism operates through processes.'
findings.truth: The novel contains open racism, racial slurs and police brutality; Penguin's own KS4 pack lists 'Police Brutality' and 'Interpersonal and Institutional Racism' as themes, and teachers are advised to omit slurs when reading aloud. Structural racism is the deeper theme, but it is not the only racism in the book. The lesson also contradicts itself two paragraphs later ('Leon encounters it in school, on the streets ...').
findings.evidence: https://www.penguin.co.uk/about/social-impact/lit-in-colour/teaching-resources/my-name-is-leon-ks4 ; https://www.nate.org.uk/2026/02/06/why-we-switched-to-my-name-is-leon-at-gcse-and-why-you-should-too/

findings.claim: Practice questions labelled '30 marks - Extract Analysis' (6 of them) and '30 marks - Extended Response' / '30 marks - Essay with SPaG'.
findings.truth: AQA 8702 Paper 2 Section A is one closed-book essay chosen from two on the studied modern text, 30 marks + 4 SPaG, with NO extract printed. 'Extract Analysis' is impossible here. All 42 labels standardised to '30 marks - Modern Text Essay', matching the precedent set in english-literature-aqa__a-taste-of-honey.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md, 'Specification at a glance': 'All assessments are closed book'; 'Section A Modern texts: students will answer one essay question from a choice of two on their studied modern prose or drama text.'

findings.claim: 'During the riots, Leon experiences a moment of epiphany ... he understands ... that it is not just about Jake, but about a whole system that sees him as less valuable because of his skin colour.'
findings.truth: In the novel Leon slips out to find Jake, is caught in the disorder, and helps Tufty and the injured Mr Devlin get home; de Waal keeps his understanding limited and does not give him a political awakening. Two options: (a) soften to a reading ('the scene can be read as ...'), which keeps the analysis and needs one sentence changed plus one flashcard; or (b) cut the epiphany claim and replace it with what Leon actually does in the riot. Recommend (a).
findings.evidence: https://litbug.com/my-name-is-leon-summary/ (riot sequence); the novel's sustained child-limited focalisation.

findings.claim: Lessons 2-4 are titled 'Part 1 / Part 2 / Part 3' and the body text repeatedly says 'Part 1 opens ...', 'in Part 2', 'Part 3 intensifies'.
findings.truth: The novel has no parts (see F13). Options: (a) leave the three phases as an explicit teaching frame, now that F13 states this in lesson 6 - no ripple, no re-narration; or (b) re-title the three lessons by chapter range and rewrite every 'Part n' reference, which touches lesson titles and dozens of narration blocks across four lessons. Recommend (a).
findings.evidence: Publisher extract (dated chapters, no part headings); 42 chapters.

findings.claim: 'She calls him "sweetheart."' presented as Maureen's characteristic word, and quoted as a flashcard answer.
findings.truth: Not verifiable from any source I could reach. In chapter 1 it is the hospital NURSE who says 'All right, sweetheart?'. Either verify against the text or replace with a verified Maureen detail (the biscuit tin, or 'Memories are what I like. Things that really happened.'). Recommend replacing on the next content pass.
findings.evidence: Novel chapter 1 (publisher extract); https://www.gradesaver.com/my-name-is-leon/study-guide/quotes (verified Maureen line).

findings.claim: Jake is adopted by 'a middle-class adoptive family' / 'a middle-class family who can provide material comfort' / 'Jake's adoptive family is middle-class and comfortable'; a knowledge-check match keys 'Class inequality' to 'Jake adopted into middle-class comfort'.
findings.truth: Sources describe the adopters only as 'a young white couple'. The class reading may be supportable from the text, but I could not verify it, and it currently carries a knowledge-check answer. Recommend a text check before the class strand is kept.
findings.evidence: https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/kit-de-waal/my-name-is-leon/ ; https://litbug.com/my-name-is-leon-summary/

findings.claim: 'The novel opens with nine-year-old Leon living with his mother Carol and baby half-brother Jake.' Knowledge check keys Leon's age at the start as 'Nine'.
findings.truth: Chapter 1 (2 April 1980) is set in the hospital and has Carol say 'He's nearly nine. Eight years and nine months.' Leon turns nine that July. Every study guide and the publisher blurb say 'nine-year-old Leon', and 'Eight' is not among the options, so the key stays correct. Not worth an edit.
findings.evidence: Novel chapter 1 (publisher extract).

findings.claim: 'a nine-year-old is fighting an entire institutional system alone' (during the July 1981 riots).
findings.truth: Leon's birthday is 5 July 1971, so he is ten by the riot. The unit follows the publisher blurb in calling him nine throughout; correcting one instance would be inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Novel chapter 1 (publisher extract): 'my birthday is on the fifth of July nineteen seventy-one'.

findings.claim: KC 'How does racism primarily operate in the novel?' keyed to 'Through structural systems and processes', with 'Through overtly racist characters' and 'Through explicit racial slurs' as distractors.
findings.truth: After F15 those distractors are arguably also true of the novel, but 'primarily' keeps the key defensible and structural racism is the dominant theme. Left as it stands.
findings.evidence: Penguin KS4 theme list.

summary: Seven lessons checked; 23 findings (11 HIGH, 8 MEDIUM, 4 LOW: 16 FIX, 4 ADJUDICATE, 3 NOTE), 111 edits. The unit carries a cluster of invented character facts: Maureen is described as Jamaican-British and as the source of Leon's Caribbean identity (she is white; that is Tufty's role), Tina is presented as the social worker (she is Carol's neighbour; the social worker is Salma), the allotment is called Maureen's garden, Leon is said to have ongoing contact visits with Jake (contact ends at the adoption), and he is placed at Maureen's during the riots (he is at Sylvia's). Lesson 1 quotes a fabricated dedication and an invented riot trigger; lesson 6 claims a three-part structure and present-tense shifts (42 dated chapters, present tense throughout). All 42 practice questions were relabelled: six said 'Extract Analysis' on a paper that prints no extract. Lesson 2 is clean apart from the shared label fix.
